name: Taozhe Li
headline: Perception. Autonomy. Real-world systems.
intro: I’m a Computer Science Ph.D. student at the University of Oklahoma, working on visual perception, end-to-end autonomous driving, and SLAM. I build learning-based systems in Python and C++, and optimize models for deployment on NVIDIA platforms.

experience.description: Research in dynamic SLAM, camera-based autonomous driving, and visual perception. Work includes dataset collection, multi-sensor calibration, model deployment on NVIDIA boards, and CUDA optimization.

Cleaned training and evaluation data, trained object detection models, and deployed them on robots for detection and localization. Improved model efficiency by 37.3% with less than 1% loss in accuracy, using Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, C++, and ONNX.
Flight Mechanics (AME3333, Spring 2025), Statics (AME2113, Fall 2025), and Robotics Lab (AME4802, Spring 2026).

projects.title: End-to-End Autonomous Driving
projects.description: Exploring Vision-Language-Action models and unified driving architectures for perception, scene understanding, prediction, reasoning, planning, and action generation.
projects.contribution: Studying and implementing architectures including UniAD, OpenEMMA, OpenDriveVLA, and DriveVLA-W0.

projects.title: Occupancy Prediction & BEV Detection
projects.description: Built a multi-camera perception workflow spanning data collection, model evaluation, and deployment.
projects.contribution: Calibrated and synchronized six surround-view cameras with LiDAR, curated occupancy and BEV datasets, evaluated and modified models, and optimized inference using CUDA on Jetson AGX Orin and NVIDIA Thor.

projects.title: Camera-Based Driving Perception
projects.description: Developed visual perception and end-to-end driving components for a surround-camera autonomous driving system.
projects.contribution: Responsible for visual perception and end-to-end driving algorithms, implemented in C++ and Python.

projects.title: Dynamic SLAM
projects.description: Addressed the degradation of traditional SLAM systems in dynamic environments.
projects.contribution: Implemented a machine-learning-based discriminator for dynamic and static feature points, and the complete SLAM system. Evaluated on the KITTI Tracking dataset.

projects.title: YOLOv5 + DeepSORT Tracking
projects.description: Designed a pedestrian and vehicle tracking system for open-road environments.
projects.contribution: Combined YOLOv5 detection with DeepSORT tracking and built a PyQt5 interface. Received the Excellent Undergraduate Dissertation Award.

projects.title: Plant Pathology Classification
projects.description: Used EfficientNet to solve a multi-label plant disease classification problem.
projects.contribution: Placed in the top 3% on the final Kaggle competition leaderboard.
